meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (national unitary jurisdiction, no sub-state fiscal distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition; company law based on the consolidated Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion on Taxes on Income and Capital, signed 20 December 1996, as amended by Protocol of 28 May 2009
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China, signed 12 March 1994, as amended by Protocol of 8 May 2014
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and India, signed 16 December 2008
Agreement between the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) and the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments, signed 1984
Luxembourg-Switzerland Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement of 23 January 2010 (relevant for cross-border SaaS and EU market access)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Art. 40-1 et seq., SCSp regime); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 18/687 (AML/CFT compliance duties of the general partner and registered agent); Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843, as implemented; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on funds transfer transparency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority, public notary or local registry office in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate UBO or intermediate holding company on the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company registrar in the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and documentary evidence of source of wealth and source of funds of each UBO (assets and income statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or licensed financial institution in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO disclosure consent and representation letter under Art. 6 of the RBE Law of 13 January 2019, together with the organizational chart of the 25% or more ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner of the SCSp, authenticated before a Luxembourg notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every UBO, general partner and authorized signatory against: (i) consolidated EU and UN restrictive measures lists, (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (pursuant to USD payment-rail exposure via Stripe and ACH), (iii) Luxembourg CSSF PEP guidance under the AML/CFT Law (Art. 3 para. 8), and (iv) FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists; enhanced due diligence is compulsory for PEPs, and periodic re-screening is documented on each material event and on adhesion to Regulation (EU) 2023/1113.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at www.lbr.lu (e-service: RCS Online)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must include the statutory decisive formula 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'; the name may be in French, German, English or any other language using Latin script, must be distinctive and pronounceable, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in the RCS; no non-Latin script is permitted without official transliteration into Latin characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative name-clearance decision, the applicant through counsel may either (i) immediately submit an amended name application via the LBR portal without penalty, or (ii) file a written reasoned appeal with the Commercial Chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 15 days of the date of notification of the rejection, attaching the RCS refusal certificate and evidence of distinctiveness; no temporary inscription is granted during the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible: the RCS requires a real and physical Luxembourg registered address; domiciliation by a licensed professional of the financial sector (PFS) or a law-firm-managed suite is accepted market practice, but a pure mail-forwarding virtual office without an executed service contract and managed premises does not satisfy the substance expectations of the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD) and may result in RBE updating orders; registered address, business agent and substance folders must be evidenced.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 5-8% probability within the first 12 months for a low-risk PropTech SaaS SCSp; probability materially increases (up to 30%) where the registered address is a mass-domiciliation hub or where unusual related-party flows or VAT refund patterns trigger ACD and CCSS desk controls and unannounced on-site visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 1-24; SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013, within Title II, Chapter V (Société en commandite spéciale).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société / Convention de commandite spéciale) executed by all partners, filed with RCS Form C (dépôt d'acte).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no escrow requirement; partners freely determine contributions in cash, in kind, or in industry, and the default capital of the SCSp may be zero until contributions are actually made.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the SCSp under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, is hereby approved, and the General Partner confirms each limited partner's subscription to the contributions set forth in the Partnership Agreement. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership is fixed at the address indicated in the agreement, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that the General Partner appoints [Name] as designated manager with the powers and remuneration determined by the General Partner, and authorizes the manager to complete all filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to register the beneficial owner with the RBE register, and to open and operate bank accounts on behalf of the Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal, RCS name index
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior search of the RCS register to verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg entity. Submit an electronic name clearance request; the legal name must include the words 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'.
required_dossiers: Proposed name in three priority variants
Identity document and full address of the proposed General Partner
Brief description of the partnership's object
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged, promptly file an alternative name variant with a written explanation of distinguishing elements; no statutory objection period applies at this preliminary stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and limited partners, optionally assisted by a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement containing corporate name, registered office address, object, duration, capital contributions and profit-sharing rules, rights and obligations of the General Partner and limited partners, and transfer restrictions. Execute the agreement by private deed; to obtain a 'date certaine' (certified date), register the deed with the Registration Administration, use a registered letter, or pass a notarial deed if recommendation from lenders or counterparties exists.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of all partners
Proof of residential address of each partner
Signed pages of General Partner and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is contested or formal defects are identified, the partners may amend the agreement by private deed and re-execute; any rectification must be signed by all partners and re-deposited with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Partnership Agreement and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS, filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File electronically via lbr.lu: upload the signed partnership agreement, RCS Form C, evidence of registered office, and identity documentation. Pay the official filing fee of approximately EUR 75. Once examined, the Registrar assigns a unique RCS registration number and issues a certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered office address (lease or occupancy proof)
Identity papers and signed powers of attorney of filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or formal deficiency, cure within 15 working days by filing supplementary declarations or amended signatures; no adverse effect on the partnership's internal validity occurs, and third-party effectiveness attaches upon completed registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RESA publication service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, LBR automatically publishes the registered particulars in RESA within the statutory publication window. Verify the published extract contains the correct name, legal form, registered office, and identity of the General Partner; no separate filing by the applicant is required.
required_dossiers: Publication draft auto-generated by the RCS system
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains errors, file a request for rectification with RCS within one month of the erroneous publication; the rectification is also published at the entity's cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filing: RBE Beneficial Owner Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), held and administered by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial owner declaration identifying all natural persons holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the partnership interests or control. Submit through the LBR online portal; obtain the RBE registration number and schedule an annual confirmation.
required_dossiers: Proof of authority of the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is late, file immediately with an explanation; administrative fines up to EUR 1,250 per month of delay may apply, and a written waiver request may be submitted to the RBE supervisory authority in cases of force majeure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) - GIfS; no sectoral operating permit required for cloud-based software and property management platform services under ISIC 6201.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license required; general freedom of establishment applies for electronic and software services in Luxembourg.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity consists of office-based software development and cloud data processing, not a classified installation (établissement classé) under the Law of 9 May 2022 on classified establishments; no full EIA report or registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core SaaS activity; any office wastewater discharge follows municipal sewer regulations; energy use of the PropTech platform relies on third-party data centers in the EU Green Deal reporting framework, with no direct VOC or industrial wastewater emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises require a fire safety conformity certificate from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); electrical installation inspection per ILNAS guidance; structural load approval per municipal building code; occupational workplace filing with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); no industrial clearance applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes - ACD) for direct taxes and the Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AEDT) for VAT. Official portals: myguichet.lu and backoffice.etat.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors must first file the SCSp constituent deed and articles of association with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a notary, obtain the 6-digit Luxembourg business registration number (matricule), appoint at least one Luxembourg resident manager, then apply to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT identification number. The ACD uses the same matricule for corporate and partnership tax files.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. An SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg income tax purposes and is not itself subject to corporate income tax or net wealth tax; profits and losses are allocated to and taxed at partner level. For VAT/SaaS supplies, the SCSp is the taxable person supplying electronic services, subject to the normal place-of-supply rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no general check-the-box election for an SCSp; Luxembourg statutory law prescribes tax transparency. Limited elections/regimes available include the Luxembourg VAT group election (tax unity) for related Luxembourg taxable persons, and the anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law that must be observed to prevent deduction/no-inclusion outcomes. An SCSp cannot elect to be treated as an opaque corporate entity for Luxembourg tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover excluding VAT for most supplies of goods and services. For EU cross-border distance sales and B2C digital services, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies, requiring registration or use of the EU One-Stop-Shop above that threshold; non-established third-country suppliers of digital services normally have no threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based tax control mandate. Invoices must comply with VAT Directive rules and the Luxembourg VAT law; electronic invoicing is permitted and accepted as standard. For B2G transactions, e-invoicing in PEPPOL-BIS 3.0 format is required for Luxembourg public entities, with mandatory e-archiving and accessibility for the tax authorities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Luxembourg applies 0% VAT to physical exports of goods where the goods are dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU, supported by export proof. Export of B2B SaaS/cloud services to taxable customers established outside the EU is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and qualifies for zero-rating if the customer is a non-EU taxable person and no EU effective-use nexus arises; intra-EU B2B services are taxable at the customer's place of establishment, requiring normal invoicing and Intrastat/OSS reporting where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/UA or electronic export declaration via the EU Customs Single Window)
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill evidencing dispatch from the EU
Commercial invoice with an export reference and proof of sale
Proof of payment / bank transfer, and where requested, Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may require substantiation of export zero-rating; failure to provide valid transport, customs, and payment documentation within the requisite period triggers reassessment at the standard Luxembourg VAT rate of 17%, plus default interest, late-payment penalties of up to 20% of the VAT due, and a 10% corrective penalty for under-declared VAT. Fraudulent export zero-rating can give rise to criminal fines of EUR 1,000 to EUR 25,000, confiscation of goods, and partner/manager personal liability; retrospective clawbacks apply for five tax years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or bad faith.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem, is the central bank and the competent balance-of-payments statistical authority. Prudential supervision of credit institutions and AML/CFT conduct oversight are concurrently exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg has no separate national foreign-exchange control authority, as capital and payment liberalisation is governed by the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and CSSF/BCL joint circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full liberalisation of both capital and current-account transactions under Articles 63–66 TFEU and EU Capital Movements Directive 88/361/EEC, as implemented. The euro is fully convertible, with no compulsory licensing, prior-approval, surrender, or repatriation requirements for capital or profit flows. An SCSp is tax-transparent, so profit distributions flow directly to partners without Luxembourg withholding tax; residual remittance hurdles arise only from the partner-resident jurisdiction's tax, FATCA/CRS, or local anti-money-laundering rules. The EU safeguard clause for non-EU capital movements is legislatively available but is not currently engaged for routine cross-border SaaS subscription revenues or foreign partner capital injections.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, mandatory conversion ratio, or minimum repatriation percentage applies in Luxembourg. Exporters and SaaS service providers may freely invoice, receive, hold, and convert foreign currency receipts. The only binding compliance obligation is ex-post statistical declaration of cross-border transactions to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes, triggered individually or in aggregate at the EUR 12,500 per-transaction threshold, plus standard tax filings such as VAT recapitulative statements and Intrastat reporting where the underlying scope applies. The SCSp's platform revenue from PropTech software subscriptions is classified as services (ISIC 6201) and is not subject to goods-export surrender regimes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account for SaaS subscription collections
Operational Account and USD concentration account for cross-border software revenues
Capital Escrow Account and treasury/FX hedging line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High-to-moderate feasibility under EU PSD2 passporting. A CSSF-licensed electronic money institution or an EEA-passported EMI may lawfully open settlement, collection, and disbursement accounts for the SCSp without full commercial-bank credit underwriting, and may process the target Stripe_Billing and ACH_Direct rails. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs are legally constrained in Luxembourg because CSSF-regulated banks will not recognise them as qualified payment-system participants for capital deposits, FX conversion, or sub-account maintenance, and the SCSp would face UBO transparency and source-of-funds rejection at the receiving Luxembourg bank. The recommended structure is dual: (i) a CSSF-licensed or EEA-passported EMI for the ACH/USD collection concentration overlay, and (ii) a Tier-1 Luxembourg commercial bank for the EUR operational and capital escrow accounts, with daily treasury sweeps between them.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML/CFT law (Law of 19 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02) does not statutorily mandate an in-person interview for low-risk corporate clients. Remote onboarding is permitted where the client is verified through CSSF-accepted e-identification means (eIDAS-qualified certificates, LetzKey or Luxembourg national eID, video-verified identification) and the corporate KYC file is supported by notarised or apostilled documents. In practice, BCEE and BIL require at least one video meeting with the managing general partner's authorised director or designated money-laundering-reporting officer to attest signatory powers, economic rationale, and source of funds; purely documentary remote opening is uncommon for partnerships with non-resident limited partners. For the LU_SCSP, the general partner, a Luxembourg-registered entity, must designate a director to attend the initial onboarding meeting, either physically or via institutional-grade videoconference, and the SCSp's partnership agreement must be lodged in the RCS extract file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear UBO chain for foreign limited partners, particularly non-EU individual or corporate beneficiaries of the SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete uplifted ownership chain from the SCSp to every ultimate natural person; Luxembourg RCS UBO register filing confirmation; notarised or apostilled passport copies for all UBOs; notarised power-of-attorney or manager resolution for corporate general partners; CSSF-compliant UBO declaration form; independent PEP and adverse-media screening reports; written explanation of the commercial purpose of each LP interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial capital injection, amplified by the SCSp's zero statutory minimum capital requirement which invites scrutiny of the intended funding mix.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: At least 12 months of bank statements from the contributing partner; signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds questionnaire; executed capital commitment and contribution letters; audited or management financial statements of any corporate contributing partners; a funds-flow schedule tracing the injection route from origin to the Luxembourg bank; written confirmation that no crypto-asset, unregulated lending, or unexplained cash precedes the contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or negative-media flags on partners or on PropTech SaaS customers receiving software services from the platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions-screening evidence (EU consolidated list, OFAC SDN, UN security council) covering all UBOs and major counterparties; a commercial rationale memorandum describing the real-estate property management cloud use case; business-partner due-diligence files for B2B SaaS customers; negative-news search reports with dates and sources; end-user licence agreements confirming the non-financial nature of the software; a rapid adverse-media remediation process and, where required, a legal opinion on the legitimate business purpose of the flagged relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the statutory license-free status (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390) and bank expectations that a SaaS/PropTech platform may conceal regulated payment or lending activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Luxembourg avocat legal opinion confirming that the SCSp's core activities do not trigger MiFID II, PSD2, EMI, or alternative-investment-fund licensing; CSSF pre-confirmation or confirmation letter where the activity touches payment aggregation; product and technical documentation showing the platform is non-custodial and merely feeds subscription charges through Stripe Billing and ACH Direct; bank reference from the parent or founder entity where available; audited or reviewed financial statements showing revenue exclusively from software subscriptions and referral fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flow concentration through a single payment aggregator (Stripe_Billing and ACH_Direct), triggering money-laundering-typology profiling of pooled settlements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Stripe merchant and payment facilitation agreements with SOC 2 or equivalent audit attestations; the SCSp's own B2B customer KYC and negative-news screening policy; chargeback, refund, and dispute management documentation; transaction-monitoring and velocity-check rationale; treasury policy describing daily conversion and sweep of USD ACH proceeds into the Luxembourg EUR operational account; contractual evidence that the SCSp never accepts cash and does not act as an unlicensed payment institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for non-resident partner contributions: the contributing partner instructs a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 interbank transfer for high-value contributions) from its bank to the SCSp's EUR operational or capital escrow account at BCEE, BIL, or Société Générale Luxembourg, with field 70 remittance information stating 'Capital contribution – Article [X] of the SCSp partnership agreement – ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS platform'. The Luxembourg receiving bank declares the transaction to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics where the per-transaction aggregate threshold of EUR 12,500 is met. For injections exceeding EUR 50,000, the CSSF AML file must evidence a continuous source-of-funds trail and the partner bank's transfer confirmation. Non-EUR injections, particularly USD, are converted by the receiving bank under standard FX execution at the prevailing ECB reference rate, with no BCL surrender or licensing obligation. For inbound US ACH collections, the recommended routing is through a US-based USD concentration account (or Stripe Treasury settlement account) followed by a same-day SWIFT MT103 credit to the Luxembourg EUR account using purpose code 'ISIC 6201 SaaS subscription revenues / B2B software services', ensuring the funds are classified as current-account services rather than capital movement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails are as follows: (1) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for high-value vendor payments, profit distributions to partners, and non-EUR disbursements in USD, GBP, or CHF; (2) SEPA Credit Transfer and MT101 batch instructions for routine disbursements such as cloud-hosting fees, subcontractor payments, and payroll through the operational account; (3) UCP600-compliant commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit for any physical Proptech hardware resale or escrow-linked vendor obligations; (4) FX spot or derivative settlements through approved EU investment firms or the relationship bank's treasury desk, subject to EMIR and MiFID II reporting. The unique clearing bottleneck is ACH_Direct: as a US NACHA rail, ACH cannot be cleared by Luxembourg banks; therefore the SCSp must maintain either a US physical-bank account or a US-licensed EMI/Stripe account as a concentration overlay, with daily treasury sweeps to Luxembourg to avoid prolonged foreign balance exposure and to align with the EUR operating currency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP deliverable FX forwards under IFEMA or ISDA 1992 master agreements, documented through the Luxembourg bank treasury desk, with the general partner expressly authorised by the SCSp partnership agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible emerging-market currency exposures arising from partner capital calls or vendor payments; permissible but subject to EMIR classification of the SCSp as a non-financial counterparty below clearing thresholds, with mandatory risk-mitigation and trade-reporting obligations.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term hedging of USD-denominated ACH subscription streams or foreign partner capital contributions, executed under an ISDA Credit Support Annex with adequate collateral documentation.
Vanilla FX options (put and call) for downside protection on subscription revenues in USD and GBP, purchased only from regulated EU investment firms or Luxembourg credit institutions.
Daily FX spot conversion of US ACH proceeds into EUR through the concentration-account overlay, executed as a standing instruction to the Luxembourg bank to neutralise conversion-rate leakage.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% base Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) plus 7% solidarity surcharge, producing an aggregate CIT rate of 22.47%; with municipal business tax (communal trade tax) at the Luxembourg City multiplier of 6.75%, the combined statutory burden is 29.22%. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, so the CIT is imposed at partner level on each partner's allocable share of the PropTech SaaS income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg IP box (80% exemption of qualifying net IP income), participation exemption (100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains), notional interest deduction on equity, exemption of municipal business tax for transparent partnerships not carrying on a commercial activity, and absence of Luxembourg withholding tax on ordinary interest. A transparent SCSp allows non-resident partners to access treaty rates on Luxembourg-source income only where real economic substance is maintained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and Form 200 (communal business tax declaration); mandatory electronic filing via the MyGuichet.lu portal and the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) e-filing system. The annual return package includes the CIT computation, solidarity surcharge, net wealth tax schedule and the municipal business tax statement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (12-month accounting period; quarterly CIT prepayments are due on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August and 10 November of the assessment year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline: 30 June of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end. The ACD routinely grants an automatic extension to 31 December of that same year for e-filed returns; for assessment cycles 2023 and 2024 the standard grace deadline is 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification of the SCSp: company name, national identification number (NIF), registered office, principal activity code (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390), and exhaustive list of general partners and limited partners with their tax residence and percentage participation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must disclose treaty residence and attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC); for a fiscally transparent SCSp the partner's allocable share must be reported to prevent double attribution of the same profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit before adjustments: net accounting income from recurring SaaS subscription revenue, real-estate rental screening fees, Stripe billing and ACH settlement proceeds, reduced by direct operating expenses and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners include only Luxembourg-source profit allocated under the partnership agreement based on economic substance, not on cash distributions or arbitrary waterfall provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and statutory add-backs: excessive management fees, interest on shareholder loans exceeding arm's-length rates, fines, and non-documented cross-border service fees charged by foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp must itemize all related-party charges paid to foreign partners or affiliates; absence of a compliant local file triggers automatic recharacterization of such fees as constructive profit distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income: qualifying IP-box net income (80% exemption), participation-exempt dividends and capital gains, and income exempt under applicable double tax treaties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The participation exemption applies only where the foreign partner holding is at least 10% (or EUR 6 million) and the holding period, substance and anti-abuse conditions are met; shell partners are denied the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward and set-off: computation of current-year taxable base after application of available prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a transparent SCSp flow through to partners and are utilised within the partner's own carry-forward regime; the entity-level limit applied in this dossier is 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base and final tax computation: application of the 21% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge and the municipal business tax multiplier applicable to the commune of establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners subject to limited tax liability do not file the municipal business tax declaration unless the SCSp maintains a permanent establishment or taxable commercial activity in Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax due; late payment: monthly interest of 0.6% (7.2% p.a.) on unpaid CIT and municipal business tax. Failure to file: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000, automatic taxation d'office with loss of deduction and carry-forward rights, and collection enforcement by writ of execution. Intentional non-filing is prosecuted as tax fraud with imprisonment and fines under Article 402 of the Luxembourg General Tax Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions from a Luxembourg taxable entity. For a fiscally transparent SCSp, no entity-level withholding arises on distributions to partners unless the ACD treats the SCSp as opaque following an ATAD GAAR recharacterization or a corporate-taxation election. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief: 0% on qualifying holdings of at least 10% held for 12 months; LU-US and other DTA rates commonly 5% for 10%+ holdings and 15% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its residence state covering the payment year; (2) submit the official Luxembourg withholding-tax reduction request (demande de réduction à la source) to the ACD via MyGuichet.lu before the distribution date, or file a refund claim under the Form 3 procedure; and (3) prove beneficial ownership, the 12-month holding period and that the partner is not a bare conduit. Relief is granted only after ACD approval, which routinely includes an economic-substance verification of the partnership and its partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15% withholding tax on outbound IP payments covering patents, software, know-how and copyright; EU Interest & Royalties Directive provides 0% on payments to qualifying EU affiliates (25% direct ownership for 24 months); DTA rates typically 0% to 10%. Interest: no statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on ordinary bank or arm's-length loan interest; ATAD anti-hybrid and GAAR rules may recharacterize excessive, non-arm's-length or equity-like interest as constructive dividends subject to the 15% dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where the Luxembourg SCSp's controlled transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per category for goods or IP, or EUR 300,000 per category for services. Master File: mandatory where the worldwide group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000 and the Luxembourg entity's controlled transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: applicable at the EUR 750,000,000 group turnover threshold. Documentation must be produced within 45 days of an ACD request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the ACD applies an equivalent economic-substance doctrine through: (i) the amended law of 17 March 2017 requiring financing and holding entities to maintain local premises, local board decision-making, qualified directors and adequate staff; (ii) the ATAD general anti-abuse rule (Art. 6ah of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law) which permits recharacterization of artificial arrangements; and (iii) treaty and EU-Directive beneficial-ownership and limitation-on-benefits tests. A transparent SCSp claiming treaty benefits must demonstrate that the partnership and its partners have real activity, substance and decision-making power in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission or false declaration of Luxembourg-source profit from the PropTech SaaS business, artificial shifting of subscription revenue to zero-tax jurisdictions, or deliberate use of shell SCSp vehicles to conceal the beneficial ownership of real-estate screening income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 402 of the Luxembourg General Tax Code, attempted tax fraud is punished by a fine of up to EUR 250,000 or double the evaded tax, whichever is greater; completed fraud is punishable by imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years and/or the same fine; restitution of evaded tax plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest is mandatory. Repeat offenders face doubling of fines and extended custodial terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing applies: general partners and managers who knowingly organized the fraud are jointly and severally liable for the concealed tax. Luxembourg courts additionally impose travel bans, commercial-management prohibitions (interdiction de gérer) of up to 10 years, asset freezes and custodial sentences on the responsible natural persons. EU and Schengen mutual-assistance instruments enable cross-border enforcement of freeze, seizure and confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registration of the SCSp without local premises, staff or management autonomy, where the sole purpose is obtaining Luxembourg treaty benefits for non-resident investors, or where SaaS revenue is directed through the transparent vehicle without real business activity in Luxembourg (treaty and Directive shopping).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits and of the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 0% rate; the ACD recharacterizes all distributions as constructively Luxembourg-taxable and applies the 15% withholding tax plus 7.2% p.a. default interest; administrative anti-shell fines up to EUR 250,000 are imposed on the general partner; the OECD shell-entity information-exchange framework triggers automatic disclosure to the investor's home tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners are treated as tax representatives and are personally assessed for unpaid withholding tax, fines and interest. Civil restitution of repatriated profits is ordered against the partners; travel bans are issued where a partner attempts to leave the EU; criminal convictions for forgery follow where sham leases, sub-leases or employment contracts were manufactured to create artificial substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Margin Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or file the Local File within 45 days of an ACD request, absence of the Master File where group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million, or use of non-arm's-length SaaS subscription fees, mark-ups or royalty payments to related technology groups or foreign limited partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic upward adjustment of the taxable base to the arm's-length amount; penalty of 10% of the adjusted tax differential plus 7.2% p.a. interest; in flagrant cases the excess is recharacterized as a hidden dividend distribution subject to the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, generating double-inclusion and potential ATAD interest-limitation consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the tax return without verifying the underlying transfer pricing documentation are personally liable for the 10% penalty where gross negligence is proven. A Luxembourg commercial court may appoint a judicial administrator over the SCSp, prohibit the manager from engaging in commercial activity for up to 10 years, and enforce personal liability for unpaid withholding tax where the manager knew the documentation was fictitious or the agreements were backdated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Payment-Rails Non-Compliance (PropTech / Real-Estate SaaS)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly processing ACH or Stripe Billing payments originating from tax-evading landlords or shell real-estate clients, failing to file suspicious transaction reports (STRs) with the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF), or operating anonymous escrow or pass-through accounts for real-estate screening fees without performing client due diligence and beneficial-ownership verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended, institutional violations attract fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and director fines up to EUR 250,000; money-laundering predicated on tax evasion is punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment; the CSSF and the CRF may suspend the entity's payment processing, freeze its bank accounts and revoke any required professional authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are personally criminally liable for AML violations. Civil courts permit tax authorities and victims to pierce the SCSp veil and attach the personal assets of partners who knowingly controlled the payment flows; international travel bans and asset freezes are issued under EU mutual recognition; serious or repeated violations lead to permanent disqualification from serving as a director of any Luxembourg or EU-regulated company.
